findings.title: Read metrics omit bytes successfully read before a later file error
findings.contract: ReadMetrics.raw_bytes counts actual userspace bytes successfully read from raw candidates, including failed candidate copies.
findings.input: Fault shim limits the first read of block-0.json to 64 bytes and returns EIO on the next read; cold/block-0.json is absent.
findings.expected: The block is Unavailable and raw_bytes is 64.
findings.actual: The block is Unavailable; raw_files=2 but raw_bytes=0. Shim output confirms 64 bytes returned before EIO.
findings.cause: read_bounded discards its partial Vec on read_to_end error, and read_block increments raw_bytes only for Ok(bytes). The same helper also hides partial metadata reads from metadata_bytes during manifest fallback.

passing_probes: Query uses valid cold copy after invalid hot and counts both complete file reads.
Open uses valid rebuilt manifest after malformed primary and counts both complete manifest reads.
Publication rejects a preexisting dangling final-name symlink on this Linux filesystem.

observations.title: Rebuild cannot recover automatically when a shape-correct hot copy differs from an intact cold copy
observations.classification: recovery limitation; not a proven contract violation
observations.input: Three rows in two blocks; copy block-0.json to cold/block-0.json; change only events[0].id in hot block-0.json from 1 to 999; remove manifest.json; call rebuild_manifest with the original independent Publication.
observations.actual: rebuild_manifest returned InvalidData('rebuilt rows do not match independent anchor') and did not create manifest.rebuilt.json.
observations.reason: The API explicitly requires valid-cold fallback for Query, not rebuild. After the manifest is lost, only the full Anchor remains; rebuild has no independent per-block digest for selecting one of multiple shape-correct copies. It fails closed rather than publishing the wrong root. Restoring the raw block from trusted source or removing the corrupt hot copy permits retry.
